result.title: Skill-Latent Rewards: LLM-Guided Reward Formulation for Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning
result.summary: Long-horizon reinforcement learning under sparse and delayed feedback remains an open challenge. Existing return-decomposition methods redistribute episodic rewards to ease credit assignment, but they operate on raw state--action transitions and disregard the subgoal structure that governs meaningful progress in complex tasks. We propose Skill-LR, a hierarchical reinforcement learning framework in which a vision--language model identifies the agent's active subgoal at each timestep and a large language model generates a matching latent reward formulation through a two-stage prompting process. By conditioning reward signals on the currently active subgoal, Skill-LR produces stage-specific credit that evolves with the hierarchical plan, reducing temporal variance and improving sample efficiency. On multi-stage MiniGrid and BabyAI benchmarks, including DoorKey and Unlock-to-Unlock, Skill-LR converges faster and more reliably than sparse environmental rewards and strong credit-assignment baselines such as RUDDER and LaRe, demonstrating that subgoal-aligned latent rewards offer a principled path toward stable, interpretable credit assignment in long-horizon tasks.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 Skill-LR 分层强化学习框架：用 VLM 逐步识别当前子目标，再由 LLM 通过两阶段提示生成与子目标匹配的「latent reward」，在 MiniGrid 与 BabyAI 多阶段任务上加速收敛并改善信用分配。
AI.relevance_reason: 这里的 latent reward 只是子目标条件下的奖励分解，并非推理期 latent 状态，与 LVR 主线无直接关系；但其按子目标划分阶段并分配信用，可能为多阶段推理轨迹的步骤级监督与贡献分配提供线索，可供核查。
